commitResults.messageBody: Adds a reusable Codex skill for presenting repository changes as an HTML split-view diff so future review workflows can inspect changes visually within this project.
Introduces a Task model to keep descriptions and completion state together, and updates the command loop to support listing, marking, and unmarking tasks without adding extra application classes.

Chillguy classes live in the default package.

The SE-EDU Java standard requires every class to belong to a package. That package structure makes the codebase easier to organize as it grows.

Let's move Chillguy and Task into the chillguy package and update the setup guide to point at the packaged entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Agents: Add Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java work in this project follows the SE-EDU coding standard.

The standard is project-specific, so future agents need a local skill and an explicit instruction to load it before Java source work.

Let's add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill and mandate its use from AGENTS.md.

Commit work in this project follows the SE-EDU Git conventions.

Future agents need local guidance for commit subjects, bodies, and branch names so commit history stays consistent.

Let's add the seedu-git-standard skill and mandate its use before proposing or creating commit messages.

Add a project-specific test-ui skill that records console UI test cases in test/ui-test-plan.md and compares actual output against expected output.

Update AGENTS.md so future code updates refresh the UI test plan when needed and invoke the skill before finishing.

Task exposes its description and completion flag to subclasses and package code even though the state should be managed through Task methods.

Make the description final and keep both fields private so the class has a smaller surface area. This follows the code quality guideline to minimize scope and keeps future changes easier to reason about.

Chillguy.main handles startup text, input reading, command parsing, and task updates in one method. That mixes several levels of abstraction and makes the command flow harder to scan as more commands are added.

Extract the greeting, command dispatch, and individual command actions into small helpers. Name the command prefixes and separator values so the intent is visible at the point of use, following the code quality guidelines on readability, avoiding long methods, and avoiding magic literals.

Deadline and event commands assume their separator tokens are present before parsing. Inputs such as a deadline without /by can therefore throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and terminate the chatbot.

Validate the parsed command structure before taking substrings and show a friendly usage message when the input is malformed. Add UI regression tests for malformed deadline and event commands so the chatbot keeps running after these errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid commands with custom exceptions
commitResults.messageBody: Validate input before changing tasks and test recovery after errors.
Integrate input validation and recovery tests into master.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into task and exception packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All application classes share one package, obscuring their roles.
Group the task hierarchy in chillguy.task and the custom exception in
chillguy.exception to make related classes easier to find.

Keep Chillguy in the root package and src/main/java as the source root.
Update the test plan and build transcript to reflect the nested layout.

Validation: All 10 recorded UI tests pass with Java 25.
Integrate branch-A-Packages into master to group related classes into task and exception packages.
